sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Kontor Space is a small workspace operator, not a software-style asset-light platform. Its demonstrated revenue expansion is real: FY26 revenue ₹24.55 crore and post-pandemic 3-year CAGR 38.84%. The decisive uncertainty is whether deposits, fitouts and long fixed rental commitments earn acceptable incremental returns while current resources fund the next phase. At the observed 19 October 2026 ₹53.55 close, historical P/E14.58 x and after-rent EV/EBITDA 5.42 x look modest, but do not solve unverified cash/commitment and asset-confirmation questions. This is a speculative expansion/special-situation research watch, not an established growth compounder or supported purchase. BQS/GQS/IAS all remain NS for identified missing factors, not because SME status is inherently negative. Current full audit annexures, attributable centre economics and a credible funded obligations bridge would change the conclusion. No trade is proposed.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 5, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 4, P NS, L NS. REV starts 9 from the preselected FY23–FY26 post-pandemic window and is capped 8 for Medium confidence/relevant history; no second small-base deduction. BQS known contribution 4.26,80% coverage, bound 4.46–6.26; GQS known 5.65,85% coverage, bound 5.80–7.15; IAS known.80,20% coverage, bound 1.60–8.80. These are exact mathematical missing-data bounds, not estimates or rankings. No governance/funding/growth numeric override is imposed: missing factors stay NS. One-point GOV and MOAT uncertainty moves known BQS by±.40 combined; DUR and EARN move known GQS by±.35. Exact weights/contributions and all thirteen evidence audits are embedded.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The business fits and operates coworking/managed offices, collects seat or office fees and ancillary service income, and pays property rent, staff and facility costs. Deposits and fitouts are economically significant; rent FY26 ₹11.4897 crore is 46.79% of revenue. Historical locations include Thane, Pune, Fort and BKC; Fort contributes an operating property/managed-office stream, so its value cannot be added again to an earnings-based operating EV. In May 2024 management described approximately 1,230 seats across named sites and blended occupancy above 85%; these are dated statements, not current capacity. Customer-duration flexibility can be much shorter than landlord lock-ins. Latest actual occupied seats, current price per occupied seat and mature/new centre mix are ND, which is why synthetic seat equivalents in the model must not be mistaken for reported operating units.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Proximity, fitted inventory, service execution and anchor relationships can sustain local occupancy, but no strong network or switching barrier is demonstrated. FY23 top-three clients contributed 83.57% of Thane, 98.61% of Pune and 100% of Fort centre revenue; those are centre-level, not company-wide concentration statistics. Scale competitors provide relevant counterbenchmarks: Awfis reports 257 centres/about 177,000 network seats and 3,400 clients; Smartworks reports 89% mature/82% overall occupancy and 20% top-ten revenue concentration. Their normalized EBITDA must be used: Awfis Q3 FY26 ₹55 crore/14.4%, not reported Ind AS 116 ₹139 crore/36.5%; Smartworks FY26 normalized 17.5%. Periods, fitout services, owned property and operating mix differ, so Kontor 29.0% after-rent margin is not proof of a superior moat. Closest SME comparator Nukleus was sought, but primary downloads failed; no secondary figures are used to fabricate a three-peer valuation average.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Annual revenue FY21–26 is ₹3.9024, 4.0070, 9.1740, 11.0267, 19.7460, 24.5548 crore. Five-year CAGR 44.46% contains the pandemic base; the chosen three-year FY23–26 rate 38.84% still demonstrates strong expansion without selecting the best window after scoring. Absolute additions and annual growth are embedded with all historical rows. FY26 growth 24.35% slowed from FY25 approximately 79%; H1 FY26 grew 56.64% but H2 only 2.75% against its comparable half. This is a meaningful tempering fact, not enough to extrapolate a permanent collapse or apply an arbitrary second penalty. Revenue is largely rental/service growth; current centres, seats, occupancy and price/mix components are not separated. Latest TTM equals FY26 because no comparable H1 FY27 filing was available by cutoff; no unsupported annualization is used.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Accessible flex-office demand and the October Gurgaon heads of terms support a runway, but the headline opportunity does not establish returns or financing. Expansion requires fitout capital, landlord deposits, pre-opening cash and anchor-client ramp, not just adding seats to a spreadsheet. The stress model calibrates FY26 revenue to synthetic equivalent seats at ₹12,000 monthly and 85% occupancy, then assumes 0/8/15% capacity growth and 65/85/90% occupancy in bear/base/bull. This is an analytical unit-driver model, not management guidance or a reported seat count. New-seat fitouts use 50 sqftat ₹3,000/sqft, six months incremental landlord rent as deposits, no invented customer deposit financing and 4% revenue maintenance capex. Gurgaon 48,100 sqft at historical ₹3,000–4,000 fitout rates implies an optional ₹14.43–19.24 crore full-area stress, not a signed mandatory commitment. Cohort payback, occupancy ramps and attributable incremental IC remain ND; CAP NS and GQSNS are therefore necessary despite growth.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Dated promises matter more than promotional size. May 2024 management aimed for 5,000 FY25 seats and 10,000 FY26 seats; current verified seat count was not found, so delivery is unverified rather than declared missed. Actual FY26 sales growth is favorable execution evidence. The same call described the FY24 corporate loan as non-related, due-diligenced, callable andone-off; the ₹5.8 crore FY26 otheradvance lacks a borrower/term bridge and cannot simply be asserted to be the same unpaid loan. Director remuneration fell from ₹0.291 crore to ₹0.12 crore; no KMP loan balance disclosed, and Board reported no material Section 188 arrangement. Kanak Mangal holding fell 71.47% to 65.02% between March 2025 and 2026; current encumbrance is ND, not presumed pledged. Auditor resignation reason is missing; VCAappointment is disclosed and does not prove misconduct. A late unregistered property-loan charge and incomplete proceeds-to-project reconciliation warrant follow-up. July actual warrant deposits, not June approval amounts, enter the cash model.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: All six historical rows, tax-normalized earnings, cash flow versions, debt/working capital and capital proxies are embedded. FY26 after-rent EBITDA ₹7.1229 crore and EBIT ₹4.6843 crore grew, while finance expense ₹0.9746 crore nearly doubled. PAT fell ₹4.1242 to ₹2.2700 crore largely because FY25 deferred tax credit ₹1.021 crore became FY26 expense ₹0.7964 crore. At 25% normalized tax excluding other income, PAT is approximately ₹2.782 crore versus ₹2.745 crore, almostflat. H1 PAT ₹1.6881 plus H2 ₹0.7111 differs results FY ₹2.2701 by ₹0.1291, exactly disclosed prior-year tax credit; this is explained arithmetic, not evidence of manipulation. Three-year CFO/PAT 0.578 and FCFproxy− ₹10.809 crore are weak, but landlord-deposit investment and low receivable days complicate interpretation. Receivables ₹0.4679 crore are all within 6 months. Other non-current assets ₹19.6165 crore include deposits ₹11.7585, prepayments ₹2.058 and unidentified advances ₹5.8. Note 43 confirmation gaps, missing FY26 full audit/IFC/CARO, and unallocated OCL ₹7.2625 crore prevent full reliability/funding clearance. Historical FY24/25 IFC opinions are unmodified; missing audit-trail wording is not a clean finding. Minor rounding, cash flow classification and template issues are separately reconciled, not inflated into fraud.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Use an explicit after-rent operating cash/equity terminal model, with historical P/E, EV/EBITDA andbook value cross-checks, rather than force a DCF with unobserved lease/cohort schedules. October equity plus March reported debt/cash gives indicative EV ₹38.583 crore, P/E14.58 x, normalized P/E11.89 x, EV/EBITDA 5.42 x and P/B 1.16 x; dated mixing is disclosed. The model partitions actual fiscal days through 20 October 2031, includes dated July 23/29 warrant deposits once, pays interest/principal and taxes, retains deposits and required cash, and adds signed cash minus reserve to EV. Ordinary IRRs, entry prices and reverse-growth solutions are null because current financing/obligations are unverified. Non-rescue conditional returns are also null for any floor breach, including March before entry. Base/bull only breach the assumed ₹1.5 crorefloor at the starting ₹1.0777 crore; that assumption is sensitized and is not a default claim. Bear occupancy stress produces severe cash loss. Separate counterfactual March equity rescues at 50% discount and 3% fees expose dilution explicitly, not an investable target. Hurdle 12/15/18%, occupancy×exitmultiple, rent, deposits, capex, receivables, FD availability, advance recovery, optional warrants and Gurgaon stresses are embedded. Negative EBITDA has no positive multiple value; separate operational property/advance releases are not silently added.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear path is not merely multiple compression: loss of an anchor tenant lowers occupancy, fixed rent persists, collections slow, expansion deposits/fitouts still absorb cash, and discounted capital becomes necessary before recovery. At 65% occupancy with rent escalation and no capacity growth, the illustrative model reaches a peak net reserve gap near ₹14.18 crore and negative terminalafter-rent EBITDA; zeroequity recovery remains possible even after the modeled rescue. These are sensitivity results, not evidence of a present default. The contrary case is real revenue growth, improved FY26 CFO, moderate conventional leverage, short receivables and ₹2.278125 crore actual July receipts. The thesis-break variable is sustainable occupied-centre cash contribution after rent and fullcapital, especially if a major advance is not recoverable. A cheaper screen multiple does not offset undocumented essential obligations.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A multibagger forecast is not established. Five-year 5× and 10× share-price outcomes require approximately 38.0% and 58.5% annualized price growth respectively, much faster than merely maintaining FY26 reported profit. Historical sales CAGR does not translate one-for-one to per-share wealth: new seat fitouts, deposits, rent ramp, interest, taxes and warrant dilution intervene. Full conversion of verified 1.215 million warrants expands basic share count 19.66% but reduces existing holder ownership 16.43%; these percentages are not interchangeable. The remaining ₹6.834375 croreexercise receipts cannot be counted unless holders actually pay. Additional June proposal shares are not assumed allotted. Without demonstrated cohort returns and financeability, 5×/10× is speculative/unsupported, not a probability-weighted recommendation or a target derived from a huge TAM.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Prioritize eight evidence-led checks: current centre/occupied-seat reconciliation versus the dated 10,000 target; occupancy and anchor churn against management 60–65% breakeven estimate; rental commitments and customer notice mismatches; recovery/counterparty evidence for ₹5.8 croreadvances and ₹11.7585 croredeposits; complete FY26 statutory/CARO/IFC/audit trail package; financing and object-wise use of actual July receipts; reported versus optional warrant conversion/share count before expiry; and complete daily liquidity/restrictions. Falling occupancy near 65% is an investigation threshold grounded in historical management break-even and the linked stress, not an automatic sell signal. A verified unfundable obligation or material asset impairment would change gates; normal quarterly noise would not. Review when the next results/lease/issue filings appear; no reminder or recurring task is created by this report. Detailed baselines, warnings, resolution tests and source IDs are embedded.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: Hold—pending critical evidence; speculative expansion/special-situation research candidate, not an established growth compounder. Action category is research priority rather than eligible for investment consideration. BQS/GQS/IAS are all NS and excluded from point rankings because CAP/BAL andfunding/return/implementation evidence are missing; incomplete scores are not ranked at the bottom as if proven poor. No governance Avoid or funding Fail is asserted. There is no supported entry price range and no basis for a trade or position recommendation. Evidence could improve at unchanged price; aprice fall alone cannot clear G2/G3. Obtain the full current audit package, major asset confirmation/advances, centre cohorts, current lease/funding bridge and complete implementation data, then recompute under unchangedv 3.0 weights.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary source ledger contains dated original URLs, hashes, locators and limitations; evidence types distinguish verified disclosure, calculation, management statement and analyst assumption. Local safe inputs retain reproducible figures and 60 session market extracts; backups intentionally contain no issuer PDFs, OCR, HTML, images or personal identifiers. Reproduction validates calculations from preserved inputs, not fresh authentication of the originals. Open questions are material: current full audit andnote 1 policies; advances/deposits and development cohort allocation; unrestricted cash, facility conditions and actual drawability; rent maturities/unallocated liabilities; current occupancy, seat pricing and client concentration; promoter encumbrance; object-wise proceeds use; andcomplete trade/no-tradehistory. Twopeer primary comparisons are usable; Nukleus primary attempts were unavailable, so no numbers are borrowed fromnews. DCF terminalshare is NA because DCF is not used. All scenarios are assumptions with explicit sensitivities, not certainty or personalized investment advice.

summary: Kontor Space is a small workspace operator, not a software-style asset-light platform. Its demonstrated revenue expansion is real: FY26 revenue ₹24.55 crore and post-pandemic 3-year CAGR 38.84%. The decisive uncertainty is whether deposits, fitouts and long fixed rental commitments earn acceptable incremental returns while current resources fund the next phase. At the observed 19 October 2026 ₹53.55 close, historical P/E14.58 x and after-rent EV/EBITDA 5.42 x look modest, but do not solve unverified cash/commitment and asset-confirmation questions. This is a speculative expansion/special-situation research watch, not an established growth compounder or supported purchase. BQS/GQS/IAS all remain NS for identified missing factors, not because SME status is inherently negative. Current full audit annexures, attributable centre economics and a credible funded obligations bridge would change the conclusion. No trade is proposed.
